full_judgment:
3. Mr. M.L. Bhowmik, the learned Advocate has appeared along with Mr. B.K. Das, the learned. Advocate for the petitioner but none has appeared for the opposite party, the Assistant Custodian Contention of Mr. Bhowmik has been based on the decision of Division Bench of this Court reported in 21 D.L.R. 331 as already referred to above. In that case the Deputy Commissioner of a District made an application to be a party in a Probate proceeding under section 283 of the Succession Act alleging that the relevant record of rights contained a wrong entry in favour of the deceased testator who, in fact, got no interest in the property to be bequeathed by the Will but his application was rejected by the High Court on the ground that the Deputy Commissioner was not a necessary party since he got no interest in the land through the deceased testator. I have perused that decision but I find that this decision is not applicable to the instant case since the Custodian of Enemy Property, though he does not claim, interest through the deceased testator, has certainly got every interest in the "Enemy Property" which vested in him under law namely, the Defense of Pakistan Rules and thereafter vested in the Government. 

 4. Mr. B. K. Das concedes that if the property in question is an enemy property then the Custodian has got every interest therein but he has referred to the record of the instant case and has pointed out that there is no prima facie evidence that the property in question is at all an enemy property. The application of the Assistant Custodian itself shows that an Enemy Property case was started in 1978 on the basis of a report of the Tahsildar who however did not state that the deceased testator was ever an enemy alien residing in India in the relevant period; that is during the Indo-Pak. War of 1965. The report of the Tahsildar simply stated that the sons of Satish Chandra. Roy who was the recorded tenant "became his legal heirs but they are Indian nationals". Report does not even state that Satish died in India as an enemy alien or the date of his death nor does it show that the property was enlisted and treated as Enemy Property at any time before it was submitted in 1978, On the other hand, the petitioner filed a certified copy of Death Register of Begumganj Municipality to show that the petitioner's father Satish Chandra Roy died at his house in Noakhali as a Bangladeshi citizen in the year 1975. The Tahsildar's report simply shows that "sons of Satish Chandra are Indian Nationals". Even if his sons are Indian Nationals this fact does not make him an enemy alien or his property an enemy property under the Defense of Pakistan Rules. Mere claim of the Assistant Custodian that the property of the deceased testator is an enemy property in respect of which an enemy property case was started in 1978 is not sufficient for coming to a conclusion that the property is an enemy property. In these circumstances the impugned order allowing addition of party cannot be maintained but the matter may be further enquired into.
